children: told Reuters that neither the company nor the U.S. government can remotely disable customers' Maven systems, as shares traded at $195.25, down 0.48% at 10:35 a.m. ET Friday. The statement addresses a central concern for European military buyers: who controls the technology once it is deployed?

According to Reuters' reporting, NATO purchased Maven for its European military headquarters in 2025 and declared full technical operating capability in June 2026. The platform brings together battlefield information from sources including satellites and radar. Palantir's latest reported quarterly revenue reached $1.94 billion, up 93%, with U.S. revenue rising 115% to $1.57 billion. That puts European adoption alongside an already fast-growing American business.

The valuation leaves little room for complacency. A GF Score of 83/100 sits alongside a price-to-earnings ratio of 166.31, suggesting solid business metrics come with demanding earnings expectations. Customer control addresses one technical concern, but governments still have to weigh sovereignty, security and oversight. For investors, the next meaningful signals are additional deployments, renewals and disclosed contract values. Those would show whether NATO's adoption translates into a broader European business.

title: Palantir Stocks Move Lower as NATO AI Sovereignty Faces Scrutiny
